content.text:
The hydration warning is fixed. A temporary test of the issue's case fails without the change and passes with it. The existing hydration tests and the `compiler-sfc` tests (500 tests) all pass. I deleted the temporary test afterwards and didn't touch any existing tests.

**Cause:** `v-bind('props.backgroundColor')` contains a `.`, so the CSS variable name has to be escaped. During SSR it's written into the HTML escaped (`--<id>-props\.backgroundColor`). On the client, `getCssVars()` returns the unescaped name (`<id>-props.backgroundColor`). The hydration style check compared the two and reported a mismatch. It only shows up when the child's root element also has its own `:style` binding, because otherwise there's no client-side `style` prop and the style check never runs.

**Fix:**
- `packages/shared/src/escapeHtml.ts`: moved `getEscapedCssVarName` (and its regex) here from `compiler-sfc/src/script/utils.ts`, so the runtime can use it too.
- `packages/compiler-sfc/src/style/cssVars.ts`: now imports the function from `@vue/shared`.
- `packages/runtime-core/src/hydration.ts`: `resolveCssVars` now escapes each var name before adding it to the expected style map, so it matches what the server rendered.

Production builds weren't affected, since var names there are hashes with no special characters.

I didn't get a full TypeScript type-check to finish (I stopped it when it timed out). The editor did flag an unused import in `hydration.ts`, but that was just between my two edits; the function is used now.
